transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-30 09:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Skyward CTO), Lina Park (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Head of Data), Nora Feld (PM)

Summary:
Short POC scoping focused on international model shortlist for logistics domain — priorities: extraction accuracy from manifests, bilingual QA (English/Spanish with occasional Japanese), latency SLO for real-time operator assistance, and a 6-week pilot timeline. Discussed workload sizing (peak QPS ~180-220), benchmark plan, security/VPC requirements, and next steps for a microbenchmark run.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, model shortlist, quantization and latency trade-offs, data residency and SOC2, POC timeline

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone good morning, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. can you, Marco, kick us off with a quick context on what Skyward's looking to prove in this POC?

[00:00:22] Marco Ruiz: yeah sure, thanks Alex. um so goal is twofold — first, reliable extraction of fields from shipment manifests and proof-of-delivery notes across spanish and english, occasional japanese. second, operator assist chat that helps routing teams triage exceptions in near real time — like sub-300 ms ideally, 300 to 500 acceptable for some flows. overall we want to measure accuracy and real-world latency/cost.

[00:00:45] Priya Nair: got it. when you say extraction accuracy, are you measuring entity-level F1, end-to-end slot accuracy, or human-in-loop correction rate?

[00:00:53] Lina Park: primary metric is entity-level F1 for manifests, but we also care about downstream task accuracy — e.g., whether the right handling code is applied. and we want human corrections < 5% after model suggestions, that's like a success bar.

[00:01:12] Samir Patel: and on throughput — baseline is about 10k manifests per day, but peak concurrent operator sessions might generate bursty traffic up to 200 QPS for inference across the region. long-term we expect 20M tokens/day but POC can use sampled traffic.

[00:01:34] Alex Chen: great, that gives Priya what she needs for sizing. quick check — any RFP compliance items beyond SOC2 and SSO we should know?

[00:01:42] Marco Ruiz: data residency for EU shipments, yes. and we'll need audit logs and KMS integration for keys if we go private Dedicated or VPC route. also SAML SSO for console access.

[00:01:58] Priya Nair: noted. for the POC we're proposing three open-model candidates to bench — Mistral-7B (smaller high-perf), Polyglot-13B-multilang (our shorthand, it's an open 13B multilang), and Llama-2-13B-optimized variant. we can also add a quantized 70B variant if you want to test highest quality but it's heavier.

[00:02:23] Nora Feld: can you explain the trade-offs briefly? we heard from infra that anything > 32GB per replica is tricky on our current committed infra.

[00:02:31] Priya Nair: yeah so short version — smaller models (7B) are faster and cheaper but may miss subtle domain terminology in manifests, especially multilingual edge cases. 13B hits a better quality sweet spot; 70B can be higher quality for very complex instructions but requires heavy memory (usually quant/sgd tricks) and more tuning. quantization (int8/int4) often recovers most throughput gains with minimal quality loss but needs verification on your dataset.

[00:03:02] Samir Patel: when you say quantization minimal loss, is that on entity extraction? have you seen it degrade entity spans?

[00:03:09] Priya Nair: good question. it can sometimes slightly affect generation phrasing but extraction F1 typically holds up with post-processing. however for very low-resource languages or rare numeric formats we recommend running a small eval set. that's what the microbench is for.

[00:03:28] Alex Chen: let's talk numbers for sizing — Priya, based on their 200 QPS burst and token assumptions what's the cluster you'd recommend for the POC?

[00:03:36] Priya Nair: for a microbench/test POC, start with two GPU nodes (A100x2 or equivalent) configured behind Redwood Dedicated pool with auto-burst off, autoscale policy for queue depth. that supports roughly 150-220 QPS for 7B-ish models with low-latency tails. for 13B we suggest three nodes to keep p50~60ms and p95 under 350ms depending on sequence length; numbers depend on batch config and KV cache hit rates.

[00:04:02] Marco Ruiz: wanted to clarify Sequence length — manifests are token heavy sometimes — avg 512 tokens, some up to 1.5k. does that change sizing drastically?

[00:04:12] Priya Nair: yes, longer context increases compute linearly and KV cache pressure. for sequences averaging 512 we can hit those latency numbers; at 1.5k you should budget +40-60% capacity or leverage prefix caching for repeated headers. Redwood's KV cache helps a lot for repeated manifest templates.

[00:04:35] Lina Park: prefix caching — is that out-of-the-box or needs custom integration?

[00:04:39] Priya Nair: it's built into the runtime — automatic prefix detection for repeated doc headers; you can also pin templates if you have consistent formats.

[00:04:47] Samir Patel: security question — if we go VPC private deployment, can Redwood still provide metrics and tracing to your console, or is it fully customer-controlled?

[00:04:56] Alex Chen: we provide a private control plane option: Metrics can be pushed to your monitoring via secure endpoints, audit logs and traces are buffered locally and forwarded per policy. for fully air-gapped setups we hand over local telemetry bundles. details in the security pack.

[00:05:12] Marco Ruiz: ok good. about evaluation plan — what does success look like in week 2 vs week 6?

[00:05:18] Priya Nair: week 1: data ingest and baseline runs on 1k examples to validate tokenization and formatting. week 2: microbench results (latency/throughput + entity F1) and preliminary tradeoffs. week 3-4: iterate on prompt engineering, simple instruction tuning or adapters if needed, apply quantization and rerun benchmarks. week 5: operator integration tests and canary routing. week 6: decision review — quality vs cost vs latency and next steps for production.

[00:05:49] Nora Feld: timeline sounds fine. on adapters — are you recommending fine-tune or few-shot + prompt engineering?

[00:05:56] Priya Nair: prefer few-shot/prompt engineering first. if accuracy remains below threshold we can test lightweight LoRA adapters on 13B; that adds time (extra compute and training step) but often worth it for domain-specific labels.

[00:06:15] Alex Chen: cost expectations for the POC — rough ballpark for Redwood Dedicated microbench and pilot?

[00:06:21] Priya Nair: microbench cost is small — just run costs on a couple nodes, we'll share sample pricing. Pilot with 2–3 nodes across 4 weeks will be visible on the pricing template; we also show per-token operational estimate so you can project to 20M tokens/day. Alex will send SOW/pricing.

[00:06:39] Marco Ruiz: competitor question — we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints for quality; we liked Anthropic's contextual safety but costs and data residency were issues. curious how Redwood's routing/fallback works if we hit capacity.

[00:06:51] Alex Chen: Redwood supports policy-based routing — you can prefer lower-cost variants and have auto-fallback to a smaller model or a different region when capacity constrained. fallbacks can be configured per-route to preserve critical flows.

[00:07:05] Samir Patel: ok good. about multilingual coverage — do you have recommended tokenizers or model families for japanese + spanish? our current tokenization leaks with some shipping codes.

[00:07:15] Priya Nair: Polyglot-13B is specifically tuned for multi-lingual token coverage and handles ja/es well; Llama-2 variants are decent but sometimes require custom tokenizers or pre-tokenization steps for special codes. We'll validate tokenization in week 1.

[00:07:32] Lina Park: sample dataset — we'll include a few edge cases: manifest with OCR errors, encoded barcodes, mixed language comments. will that break the bench?

[00:07:41] Priya Nair: it's expected — we'll include a noisy subset in the eval to see robustness. sometimes pre-cleaning helps but you want realistic failures.

[00:07:50] Alex Chen: any legal/procurement timing constraints? Nora?

[00:07:53] Nora Feld: procurement has a month-long review for entitlements; for pilot we may need a shorter SOW with limited liability clauses. we'll get legal contacts after this call.

[00:08:03] Marco Ruiz: one more on observability — can we get token-level cost and per-route latency in the POC?

[00:08:10] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost and p50/p95 per model and per route. we'd enable tracing hooks for your staging environment.

[00:08:20] Alex Chen: ok let's walk through the benchmark plan Priya — what tests do we run in microbench?

[00:08:24] Priya Nair: three tests: 1) latency microbench with synthetic loads mimicking 200 QPS bursts, 2) accuracy eval on 1k labeled manifests (entity F1 + span match), 3) robustness test with noisy OCR samples. We'll produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens per model and quant config.

[00:08:45] Samir Patel: do you include cold-starts and cache warmups in latency?

[00:08:49] Priya Nair: yes we'll report cold and warm latencies; also show caching hit rate projected for prefix-heavy workloads.

[00:08:58] Marco Ruiz: acceptable SLOs again — p95 < 500 ms for operator chat, and entity F1 > 0.92 ideally, >0.88 minimum?

[00:09:07] Priya Nair: that sounds like a reasonable target. we'll use those as success criteria in the report.

[00:09:13] Nora Feld: any thought on human-in-loop — do you want us to route low-confidence to human?

[00:09:18] Priya Nair: absolutely. we recommend a confidence threshold with a fallback for human review, and we can instrument that to track reduction in operator time.

[00:09:25] Alex Chen: okay let's capture responsibilities — Alex will share pricing + SOW, Priya will run microbench, Skyward provides data samples and infra constraints, and we'll reconvene after microbench.

[00:09:36] Marco Ruiz: perfect. quick clarification — do you need sample PII redaction before upload? we can anonymize but prefer Redwood to receive raw samples under NDA.

[00:09:46] Alex Chen: NDA is fine; we can arrange secure S3 transfer and KMS-managed encryption. that's in the security pack.

[00:09:54] Samir Patel: great. last question — do you recommend starting hosted API or Redwood Dedicated for the POC?

[00:09:59] Priya Nair: for ramping quickly, hosted works. but given your compliance and VPC needs and focus on EU residency, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in your VPC is probably the right path for the pilot to mimic production. we can start hosted microbench then move to Dedicated nodes for the integration test.

[00:10:19] Nora Feld: that staged approach works.

[00:10:22] Alex Chen: any other questions?

[00:10:24] Marco Ruiz: no, looks good. thanks everyone.

[00:10:27] Alex Chen: thanks. we'll email the security pack and SOW draft. meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" transcribed as "K-V cash" in some snippets) — please refer to recording for exact phrasing.
